findings.title: Device limit check is not atomic and can be exceeded by concurrent requests
findings.body: CreateOrUpdateDevice counts active devices in one database session and performs the insert/upsert later in a separate session. Multiple requests for distinct device IDs can all observe a count below deviceLimit and then all insert successfully, so the configured limit is not enforced under normal concurrent anonymous traffic (or across Grafana instances). The limit check and admission of a new device need to be made atomic, for example with a transaction/locking or a database-backed reservation scheme; a concurrent integration test should cover simultaneous new-device requests.

findings.title: An unauthenticated caller can exhaust the global device limit with arbitrary device IDs
findings.body: The device ID is taken from the client-controlled X-Grafana-Device-Id header and each distinct value is persisted as a new device until the global limit is reached. An attacker can send requests with generated header values to fill all slots, after which legitimate anonymous users are rejected with ErrDeviceLimitReached while the attacker's known IDs remain admitted. This turns the setting into an easy anonymous denial-of-service vector; admission should not rely solely on an arbitrary caller-provided identifier, or should include protections such as a signed/server-issued identifier and appropriate abuse controls.
